simple.meaning: סָכַת (çâkath) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “by implication, to observe quietly.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.

definitions.full: H5535. sakath [ סָכַת ] verb be silent (Arabic id ., Lane 1389 ; Samaritan pay attention , compare Thes; Arabic = also be quiet (in General), = Syriac , a differentiated √ ?); — Hiph`il declar. shew silence: Imperative masculine singular הַסְכֵּת Deut 27:9 keep silence and listen (compare נִסְכַּת Ecclus 13:23). סַל see סלל
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root to be silent;

occurrences.englishText: Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel, saying, “Be silent and listen, Israel! Today you have become the people of Yahweh your God.
